hook: JetBlue bag fees just hit *$70*. Pack smarter.
dek: New York's hometown airline raised checked bag fees again, weeks before Thanksgiving. Here is how to fly home without paying the max.

slides.label: What changed
slides.text: JetBlue raised checked bag fees for the *second time this year*, for tickets bought on or after *November 1*.

slides.label: First bag
slides.text: At least *$50* each way, up from $39. *$55* on peak dates if you prepay. *$60 to $70* if you wait until the final 24 hours.

slides.label: Second bag
slides.text: From *$70* off-peak and *$75* peak. Up to *$85* if you pay at the airport.

slides.label: Why it hurts NYC
slides.text: Every December, JFK flights to *Santo Domingo, Santiago and San Juan* are packed with gifts for family. Two bags round trip can add *$200+*.

slides.label: Beat the fees
slides.text: *Prepay early*, never at the gate. Check if your card gives a *free bag*. Weigh it at home. Price the *full trip*, bags included.

slides.label: The Den's take
slides.text: Bag fees are part of the ticket now. *Plan your bags the day you plan your flight.*

question: How many bags are you flying home with this year?
yt_title: JetBlue Bag Fees Up to $70: How to Pay Less This Holiday
caption_instagram:
JetBlue bag fees just went up again, weeks before Thanksgiving. ✈️

For tickets bought on or after November 1, a first checked bag costs at least $50 each way (it was $39). It is $55 on peak dates if you prepay, and up to $70 if you wait until the final 24 hours. A second bag starts at $70 and can hit $85 at the airport.

If you fly home to the DR or Puerto Rico every December with a suitcase full of gifts, two bags round trip can now add $200+.

How to beat it: prepay early, check your card for a free bag, weigh it at home and price the full trip with bags included.

How many bags are you flying home with this year? 👇

caption_linkedin:
Ancillary fees keep climbing ahead of peak travel season. JetBlue raised checked bag fees for the second time this year: at least $50 for a first bag on tickets bought on or after November 1, up to $70 in the final 24 hours on peak dates, and up to $85 for a second bag at the airport. The airline cites fuel and operating costs.

For travelers, the takeaway is to price the total trip, not the base fare. For businesses, it is a reminder that unbundled pricing works only as long as customers feel the add-ons are fair.
